title: The Worst Table in the Room. Audrey Hepburn Sat There Twice.
title_alternatives: The Worst Table in the Room. Audrey Hepburn Sat There Twice.
Forty Years at One Corner Table, and Nobody Noticed Any of It
A Marriage Refused, a Factory Closed, and Audrey Hepburn Alone
Table Nine Was by the Service Door. Here Is What Happened There.
The Table Was Sold in 1994. It Is Still in Somebody's Kitchen.
description:
The table was in the corner by the service door, which is the worst position in any restaurant. It was numbered nine on a plan drawn up in 1949 that nobody ever revised. It seated two comfortably and four badly. The owner gave it to people he did not know, people who arrived alone, and people who had not booked.

This is forty years at that one table.

In October 1953 a man of about fifty sat there for two hours, ate almost nothing, and asked three times whether anybody had telephoned. Nobody had. He never came back and nobody ever found out who he was waiting for.

In March 1954 a young woman came in alone at half past six, which is too early for Romans to eat and therefore the only time the place was quiet. She read typed pages while she ate. The waiter was seventeen and had been there three weeks and did not know who she was, because in March 1954 nobody did yet. What he remembered forty years later was not her face.

In June 1959 two men sat there for four hours and closed a factory in Terni, and two hundred and six people lost their jobs, and the kitchen noticed only that they kept the table a long time.

In 1962 a proposal of marriage was refused there, and then both of them had to sit and finish, because the food had already been ordered.

In 1971 a girl of nine did her homework there every weekday for a school year. She has by far the strongest claim on that table of anybody in this story, and her memory of it is that the service door hit her chair.

And in November 1988 the same woman came back, thirty-four years later, and was given the corner because it was the only table that would take four at short notice — which is the same reason she was given it the first time.

This story is a work of fiction. The restaurant, the table, the waiter and every detail in it are invented, created for storytelling and not drawn from any record.
